strings.name: Christine Sinclair
strings.summary: Sinclair scored 190 goals for Canada, establishing an international scoring record, and helped her country win Tokyo Olympic gold and two Olympic bronzes. She also won titles at Portland university and professional clubs and captained the Thorns for many years. Her international career ended in 2023 and club career in 2024; her public influence extends to women's sport and opportunities for young people.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: An Olympic champion and record international goalscorer who advanced Canadian women's football.

strings.highlights.h1.title: 190 international goals
strings.highlights.h1.text: Scored 190 goals in 331 internationals, establishing the international scoring record.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied and played at the University of Portland, winning NCAA titles in 2002 and 2005.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Olympic and club champion
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won Tokyo Olympic gold with Canada and three NWSL championships with Portland.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Promoted within Order of Canada
strings.timeline.t1.text: Appointed Companion, the order's highest grade, for sporting and public contributions.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Thorns Hall of Fame and jersey retirement
strings.timeline.t2.text: Became the club's first Hall of Fame inductee; her number 12 was retired.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Ended club playing career
strings.timeline.t3.text: Retired from the Portland Thorns after the 2024 season.
strings.timeline.t4.title: International farewell
strings.timeline.t4.text: Played her last Canada match in Vancouver.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Tokyo Olympic gold
strings.timeline.t5.text: Helped Canada win the Olympics held in 2021 after postponement.
strings.timeline.t6.title: International scoring record
strings.timeline.t6.text: Passed Abby Wambach's record of 184 international goals.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joined Portland Thorns
strings.timeline.t7.text: Joined for the inaugural NWSL season and helped win the championship.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First NCAA championship
strings.timeline.t8.text: Helped Portland win the national college title, repeating in 2005.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Senior international debut
strings.timeline.t9.text: Began playing for Canada's senior team at 16.
